questions.question: Which Indian cricketer was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendra Singh Dhoni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahendra Singh Dhoni** was inducted into the prestigious **ICC Hall of Fame** in **June 2025**, recognizing his significant contributions to international cricket and his exceptional leadership skills.
 
• Dhoni is widely regarded as one of the most successful captains in cricket history, having led India to victory in three major ICC tournaments: **ICC T20 World Cup 2007**, **ICC Cricket World Cup 2011**, and the **ICC Champions Trophy 2013**.
 
• Under Dhoni’s captaincy, the Indian cricket team achieved the **number one ranking in Test cricket** for the first time in December 2009.
 
• Dhoni is celebrated for his calm demeanor under pressure, earning him the nickname "**Captain Cool**." His ability to finish games and his tactical acumen made him an indispensable player for India.
 
• His induction into the ICC Hall of Fame highlights his **lasting legacy** in cricket and his role in elevating Indian cricket to unprecedented heights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICC Hall of Fame:**

 
 
• The ICC Hall of Fame was launched in **2009** to honor cricketers who have made significant contributions to the game and left a lasting impact.
 
• It recognizes players from all eras of cricket, spanning over 100 years of history.
 
• The inductees are chosen by a panel consisting of cricket historians, former players, and ICC officials.
 
 
 
• **Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s Career Highlights:**
 
 
• Dhoni made his international debut in **2004** against Bangladesh and quickly rose to prominence with his aggressive batting and exceptional wicket-keeping skills.
 
• He scored **10,773 runs** in ODIs, including **10 centuries**, and remains one of the most consistent finishers in cricket history.
 
• In T20Is, Dhoni played **98 matches** and scored over **1,600 runs** as a middle-order batsman.
 
• Dhoni also captained **Chennai Super Kings (CSK)** to multiple Indian Premier League (IPL) titles, further cementing his status as an iconic leader.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Inductees in ICC Hall of Fame:**
 
 
• Previous Indian players inducted include **Sunil Gavaskar**, **Kapil Dev**, **Anil Kumble**, and **Rahul Dravid**.
 
• The Hall of Fame also includes legendary international players like **Sir Donald Bradman**, **Muttiah Muralitharan**, and **Jacques Kallis**.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for ICC Hall of Fame Induction:**
 
 
• Players must have retired from international cricket for a minimum of **five years**.
 
• Their contribution to the game, achievements, and influence on cricket are considered during the selection process.
 
• Inductees are celebrated for their sportsmanship, leadership, and impact on the sport’s development globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s Legacy:**

 
 
• Dhoni’s captaincy is often praised for instilling a **fearless approach** in the Indian cricket team.
 
• He promoted young talent, such as **Virat Kohli** and **Ravindra Jadeja**, ensuring a smooth transition of leadership.
 
• His **unorthodox wicket-keeping** style and sharp cricketing instincts redefined the role of a wicketkeeper-batsman.
 
 
 
• **Post-retirement Contributions:**
 
 
• Dhoni continues to inspire future generations through his involvement in cricket and mentoring young players.
 
• He remains active in the IPL as a captain and mentor, showcasing his commitment to cricket even after international retirement.

questions.question: Which of the following global cities was officially declared the World Book Capital 2025 by UNESCO in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akkra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Accra, the capital city of Ghana**, has been officially declared as the **UNESCO World Book Capital 2025**.
 
• This prestigious designation recognizes Accra's commitment to promoting books, literacy, and reading among its citizens, particularly the youth.
 
• Accra's selection emphasizes its innovative programs aimed at **empowering the marginalized groups**, including women and young people, through reading and writing initiatives.
 
• UNESCO's decision aligns with Accra's efforts to foster inclusive education and **cultural development** through literary projects and events.
 
• The city plans to host various activities related to **book fairs, reading campaigns, workshops, and public engagement** to celebrate and promote the power of literacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO World Book Capital:**

 
 
• The UNESCO World Book Capital designation is an annual recognition given to cities that promote books and reading.
 
• The initiative began in **2001**, with Madrid, Spain, being the first city to receive the title.
 
• The program aims to highlight cities that demonstrate a commitment to fostering **literacy, education, and cultural development**.
 
• It provides an opportunity for the selected city to organize diverse events and initiatives to promote reading and celebrate literature.
 
 
 
• **Accra's Literacy Programs:**
 
 
• Accra has implemented various programs to enhance literacy rates, such as community book clubs, libraries, and writing competitions.
 
• The city actively promotes **gender equality** in literacy by providing educational opportunities for women and girls.
 
• Its focus on youth engagement ensures that the next generation is equipped with the skills needed for sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Other UNESCO World Book Capitals:**
 
 
• Previous cities that have held the title include **Madrid (2001), Bangkok (2013), Kuala Lumpur (2020)**, and Guadalajara (2022).
 
• Each city contributes unique initiatives to UNESCO's global literacy goals, enhancing the accessibility and appreciation of books.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is a fundamental human right and plays a critical role in personal and national development.
 
• Improving literacy rates contributes to **poverty reduction, gender equality, and economic growth**.
 
• UNESCO's World Book Capital program supports global efforts to achieve **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (Quality Education).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Accra, Ghana:**

 
 
• Accra is one of Africa's most vibrant cities, known for its rich cultural heritage and dynamic educational initiatives.
 
• Its designation as UNESCO World Book Capital 2025 reflects its **commitment to improving literacy and fostering a reading culture**.
 
• The city is home to numerous libraries, cultural centers, and literary organizations that work tirelessly to uplift communities through education.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO's Role in Literacy:**
 
 
• UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization) is dedicated to promoting literacy, education, and culture worldwide.
 
• The World Book Capital initiative is part of UNESCO's broader efforts to **strengthen literacy and cultural exchange**.
 
• Through this initiative, UNESCO collaborates with cities to achieve inclusive and sustainable development.

questions.question: In January 2025, which two banks signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of Assam to provide zero-premium insurance coverage to employees?

options.text: Indian Bank and Central Bank of India
Bank of Baroda and Bank of India
State Bank of India and Union Bank of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Bank and Central Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Bank** and **Central Bank of India** signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the **Government of Assam** in January 2025 to provide **zero-premium insurance coverage** to employees.
 
• The agreement aims to ensure financial security and social welfare for government employees by offering **insurance benefits** without any premium costs borne by the employees.
 
• This initiative is a part of Assam's efforts to enhance the welfare of its workforce by collaborating with banking institutions to provide **comprehensive insurance schemes**.
 
• The insurance coverage includes **life insurance and health insurance**, ensuring protection against unforeseen circumstances for employees and their families.
 
• The partnership highlights the role of public sector banks in supporting state government initiatives and promoting employee welfare through **innovative financial solutions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Bank:**

 
 
• Indian Bank is one of the leading public sector banks in India, headquartered in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It provides a wide range of financial services, including retail banking, corporate banking, and insurance services.
 
• Indian Bank has been actively involved in various state and central government initiatives for financial inclusion and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Central Bank of India:**
 
 
• Founded in **1911**, Central Bank of India is one of India's oldest and largest public sector banks, headquartered in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• The bank offers various financial products, including savings accounts, loans, and insurance services, catering to diverse customer needs.
 
• It has been a key partner in implementing government schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and Atal Pension Yojana.
 
 
 
• **Zero-Premium Insurance:**
 
 
• Zero-premium insurance is a scheme where the insured individual does not pay any premium, as the cost is borne by the employer or the government.
 
• This type of insurance is often used to provide financial protection to employees without burdening them with additional costs.
 
• It typically includes benefits such as life insurance, health coverage, and accidental insurance.
 
 
 
• **Government of Assam:**
 
 
• The Assam government has been proactive in launching welfare schemes for its citizens and employees, focusing on education, health, and financial security.
 
• Collaborating with public sector banks is a strategic move to ensure wider reach and effective implementation of such schemes.
 
• Recent initiatives include health insurance schemes for the underprivileged and financial literacy programs in rural areas.

questions.question: Which famous author released their first crime novel, *As Dark As Blood*, in January 2025?

__

• His works often delve into the life stories of prominent figures, offering readers an in-depth understanding of their personal and professional journeys.
 
• In **January 2025**, Yasar Usman released his first crime novel titled *'As Dark As Blood.'* This marked a shift in his writing style, transitioning from biographies to crime fiction.
 
• 'As Dark As Blood' is expected to be a gripping crime narrative, showcasing Usman's versatility as a writer.
 
• Yasar Usman is known for his meticulous research and storytelling prowess, traits which have been highly appreciated in his biographies. These qualities are anticipated to make his debut crime novel a success.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Yasar Usman's Previous Works:**

 
 
• Yasar Usman has authored biographies on Bollywood legends such as **Rekha**, **Rajesh Khanna**, and **Sanjay Dutt**. These books provide readers with a comprehensive understanding of the stars' lives and careers.
 
• His books are known for their unbiased approach, blending factual information with engaging storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Crime Fiction Genre:**
 
 
• The crime fiction genre typically involves narratives centered around crimes, investigations, and their resolutions.
 
• Authors in this genre often craft intricate plots to keep readers engaged and intrigued.
 
• Yasar Usman's entry into crime fiction signifies his versatility and willingness to explore new literary avenues.
 
 
 
• **Notable Crime Fiction Authors:**

• In the Indian literary sphere, authors like **Vikram Chandra** and **Abir Mukherjee** have gained recognition for their crime fiction works.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Debut Novels:**
 
 
• A debut novel often sets the tone for an author's literary career and establishes their unique style.
 
• 'As Dark As Blood' is significant as it marks Yasar Usman's first venture into crime fiction, expanding his literary repertoire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Literary Transition:** Transitioning from biographies to crime fiction showcases Yasar Usman's adaptability and willingness to explore different literary genres.
 
• **Impact on Indian Literature:** The release of 'As Dark As Blood' contributes to the evolving landscape of Indian crime fiction, bringing fresh perspectives and storytelling techniques.
 
• **Anticipated Reception:** Given Yasar Usman's reputation for detailed research and compelling narratives, 'As Dark As Blood' is expected to resonate well with readers and critics alike.
 
• **Future Potential:** Success in crime fiction could encourage Usman to further explore and innovate within this genre, adding diversity to his literary achievements.

questions.question: Which of the following indicators is included in the GoIStats app, developed by the Government of India in 2025?

options.text: Global Sports Rankings and Olympic Medal Table
National Accounts Statistics and Consumer Price Index
International Film Awards and Music Industry Data
Space Mission Launch and Satellite Deployment Data

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**national accounts statistics and consumer price index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Accounts Statistics**:

 
 
• It is a comprehensive set of data that provides information on a country's economic performance and structure.
 
• Includes GDP, GNP, national income, savings, capital formation, etc.
 
• Used for policy formulation and economic analysis.
 
• Provides insights on economic trends and sectors contributing to growth.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index**:
 
 
• Measures changes in the price level of a market basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households.
 
• Indicator of inflation and purchasing power of consumers.
 
• Essential for monetary policy decisions and cost of living adjustments.
 
• India's CPI includes components like food, housing, clothing, and medical care.
 
 
 
• **GoIStats App**:
 
 
• An initiative by the Government of India to provide real-time data and analytics.
 
• Designed to include key indicators like national accounts statistics and CPI for policy and economic planning.
 
• Provides centralized access to statistics for researchers, policymakers, and citizens.
 
 
 
• The inclusion of such indicators in the **GoIStats App** highlights the importance of tracking economic and financial metrics to ensure informed decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Sports Ranking and Olympic Medal Table**:

 
 
• Tracks performance of countries in international sports events.
 
• Used to assess sports development and participation.
 
• Not included in the GoIStats App as it does not directly relate to India's economic planning.
 
 
 
• **International Film Awards and Music Industry Data**:
 
 
• Provides information on cultural and entertainment contributions globally.
 
• Relevant for tourism and cultural exchange but not directly related to economic statistics in the GoIStats App.
 
 
 
• **Space Mission Launch Data**:
 
 
• Includes information on satellite launches and space exploration.
 
• Important for technological advancement but not typically part of economic indicators like national accounts statistics or CPI.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Accounts Statistics and CPI:**
 
 
• Essential for tracking economic growth and inflation.
 
• Used by policymakers, economists, and businesses for decision-making.
 
• Reflects the financial health of the nation and assists in fiscal planning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives:**

 
 
• The Government of India regularly updates and refines economic indicators for accurate tracking.
 
• Apps like GoIStats aim to centralize and digitize access to critical data.
 
 
 
• **Role of CPI:**
 
 
• Helps in determining monetary policies, such as interest rate adjustments.
 
• Used for indexing wages and pensions to inflation.
 
 
 
• **National Accounts Statistics:**
 
 
• Provides a detailed picture of a country's economic health and structure.
 
• Useful for international comparisons of economic performance.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transformation:**
 
 
• Integration of such data in apps like GoIStats is part of India's move toward digital governance.
 
• Ensures transparency and accessibility of statistical information.

__
 
• **D. Gúkesh**, a young Indian chess prodigy, was awarded the prestigious **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** for his achievements in chess in **January 2025**.
 
• He became one of the youngest recipients of this award due to his remarkable performance in international chess tournaments and his contribution to promoting chess in India.
 
• Gúkesh has consistently outperformed his contemporaries, achieving the status of a **Grandmaster** at a very young age.
 
• In 2022, he entered the elite **2700 Elo rating club**, making him one of the youngest players globally to achieve this milestone.
 
• His victories in several international chess tournaments have brought India recognition on the global stage in this sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**

 
 
• It is the **highest sporting honor** in India, established in **1991-1992**.
 
• The award is named after **Major Dhyan Chand**, considered one of the greatest hockey players of all time.
 
• It recognizes athletes who have demonstrated exceptional performance and brought glory to India in their respective sports disciplines.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a **medal, certificate, and cash prize of ₹25 lakh**.
 
 
 
• **D. Gúkesh's Achievements:**
 
 
• Born on **May 29, 2006**, Gúkesh hails from **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**, known as the chess hub of India.
 
• He became the **second youngest Grandmaster** in the history of chess at the age of **12 years, 7 months, and 17 days**.
 
• Gúkesh represented India in the **Chess Olympiad** and achieved exceptional results in the **2022 FIDE World Cup**.
 
• His aggressive playing style and strategic brilliance have earned him comparisons to chess legends like **Viswanathan Anand**.
 
 
 
• **Other Chess Players Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Vidit Gujrathi:** An Indian Grandmaster, known for his steady performances in global tournaments. He became a Grandmaster in **2013**.
 
• **Arjun Erigaisi:** Another young Indian chess player who has been making waves in international circuits. He became a Grandmaster at the age of **14**.
 
• **Viswanathan Anand:** A chess legend from India, the first Indian to win the **World Chess Championship**. He is a five-time world champion and recipient of the Khel Ratna Award.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Chess in India:**
 
 
• India has a rich history in chess, with the game originating in the country as **Chaturanga**.
 
• Indian players like **Viswanathan Anand** and the younger generation, including Gúkesh, have significantly contributed to popularizing chess.
 
• The government and chess federations have actively promoted the sport through initiatives, scholarships, and tournaments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**

 
 
• An athlete must exhibit consistent and exceptional performance at the **international level**.
 
• Achievements are evaluated over a four-year period prior to the year of the award.
 
 
 
• **Chess Olympiad 2022:**
 
 
• India hosted the **44th Chess Olympiad** in Chennai, marking a significant milestone in the sport's history in the country.
 
• Gúkesh was one of the standout performers, securing crucial victories for the Indian team.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India (Project Finance) Directions, 2025 have/shall come into force with effect from _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 October 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (Project Finance) Directions, 2025** are set to come into force on **1 October 2025**, as per official notifications and guidelines.
 
• The RBI introduced these directions to streamline and regulate **project financing practices**, ensuring uniformity across financial institutions in India.
 
• The directions focus on the **management of risks, financial prudence, and compliance** with existing banking norms for large-scale project financing.
 
• Key objectives include enhancing **transparency in project financing, reducing non-performing assets (NPAs)**, and fostering better financial discipline among borrowers and lenders.
 
• The implementation date of **1 October 2025** ensures adequate preparation time for banks and financial institutions to align their systems with the new directives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Financing:**

 
 
• It refers to the financing of long-term infrastructure, industrial projects, and public services based on the projected cash flows of the project rather than the balance sheets of the sponsors.
 
• Common sectors for project financing include **energy, transportation, telecommunications, water, and urban development**.
 
• Project financing typically involves **financial institutions, banks, or private equity firms**, which lend funds against future revenue streams.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI in Project Financing:**
 
 
• The RBI plays a critical role in regulating financial institutions and ensuring compliance with guidelines for project financing.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** empowers the RBI to issue directives to banks for maintaining financial discipline in project finance.
 
• RBI guidelines aim to mitigate risks such as **interest rate fluctuations, regulatory changes, and project delays**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Project Finance Directions, 2025:**
 
 
• Focus on **credit assessment and risk management** for long-term projects.
 
• Emphasis on the **use of escrow accounts** to monitor cash flows and ensure fund utilization as per project requirements.
 
• Mandatory compliance with **environmental, social, and governance (ESG)** criteria for project approvals.
 
• Introduction of **reporting frameworks** for lenders to track project progress and financial health.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Project Financing in India:**
 
 
• Major projects financed under this model include the **Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC)**, **Bandra-Worli Sea Link**, and **National Highways Development Programme (NHDP)**.
 
• These projects showcase the importance of structured financing for infrastructure development and economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation Timeline:**

 
 
• The **1 October 2025** effective date provides ample time for banks and financial institutions to adapt to the new regulations.
 
• Stakeholders, including banks and borrowers, need to ensure compliance before the deadline to avoid penalties.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Banking Sector:**
 
 
• Improved project financing practices will help reduce **loan defaults and NPAs**, fostering financial stability in the banking sector.
 
• Enhanced transparency and accountability will build trust among lenders, borrowers, and investors.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• The RBI’s authority in issuing these directions is backed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, ensuring legal compliance.
 
• The guidelines align with international best practices for project financing.

questions.question: According to the OECD Economic Outlook (Volume 2025 Issue 1), what is the projected OECD-wide inflation rate for 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.042**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **OECD Economic Outlook**: The **OECD Economic Outlook** is a key biannual publication that provides analysis and projections for member countries and other major economies. It offers insights into global economic trends and key macroeconomic indicators.
 
• **Projected Inflation Rate for 2025**: According to the **OECD Economic Outlook (Volume 2025, Issue 1)**, the proposed inflation rate for the OECD-wide region for the year 2025 is estimated to be **0.042** (4.2%). This is based on the latest economic data and forecasts.
 
• **Definition of Inflation**: Inflation refers to the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power over time. Central banks and policymakers monitor and manage inflation to ensure economic stability.
 
• **Relevance of the 4.2% Inflation Rate**: A 4.2% inflation rate indicates moderate inflation, which is generally seen as healthy for economic growth, provided it does not exceed a level that harms purchasing power and economic stability.
 
• **Global Economic Trends**: The projected inflation rate reflects ongoing economic recovery, global supply chain adjustments, and monetary policies adopted by OECD member countries. It also highlights the impact of global energy prices and geopolitical factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development)**:

 
 
• The **OECD** is an international organization comprising **38 member countries** that work together to promote economic growth, sustainable development, and global trade.
 
• Founded in **1961**, the OECD provides a platform for countries to share experiences, develop solutions, and coordinate policies on global economic challenges.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Inflation Rates**:
 
 
• **Monetary Policies:** Central banks adjust interest rates to control inflation and stabilize the economy.
 
• **Supply Chain Dynamics:** Disruptions in global supply chains can lead to higher production costs, impacting inflation rates.
 
• **Energy Prices:** Variations in oil and gas prices significantly influence inflation, as energy costs are a key component of the economy.
 
 
 
• **OECD Economic Projections**:
 
 
• The OECD regularly publishes forecasts on GDP growth, employment, inflation, and trade for its member countries and major global economies.
 
• These projections help policymakers and businesses make informed decisions based on expected economic trends.
 
 
 
• **Global Inflation Trends**:
 
 
• Many economies experienced higher inflation rates in recent years due to pandemic-induced disruptions and rising commodity prices.
 
• Efforts to stabilize inflation include tightening monetary policies and addressing supply chain challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Target Inflation Rates:** Most central banks aim for a target inflation rate of around **2%** annually. Moderate inflation promotes economic growth without significantly eroding purchasing power.
 
• **Inflation Measurement:** Inflation is commonly measured using indices such as the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** or the **Producer Price Index (PPI)**.
 
• **Impact of Inflation:** While moderate inflation supports economic activity, high inflation can reduce consumer spending, impact savings, and destabilize economies.
 
• **OECD Reports:** The OECD's economic reports serve as a valuable resource for governments, businesses, and researchers to understand and respond to global economic challenges.

• The allocation is part of India's broader strategy to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement**, aiming for significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Special focus is given to urban areas with severe pollution levels, including cities listed under the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**.

• India has pledged to reduce its **emissions intensity of GDP** by 33-35% by **2030** compared to 2005 levels.

• Major contributors include vehicular emissions, industrial activities, crop burning, and construction dust.

• The **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981** regulates air pollution control measures.
 
• The **Environment Protection Act, 1986** provides an overarching framework for pollution control in India.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• India's proactive measures, including solar energy adoption and pollution control funding, have been recognized internationally.
 
• Programs like **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** highlight India's leadership in renewable energy initiatives.

questions.question: As per Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, what was the percentage of waste processed in 2024-25, from 17.97% in 2015-16, indicating significant progress in waste management efficiency in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.807**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025**, monitors India's progress on environmental sustainability and waste management.
 
• In **2015-16**, the percentage of waste processed was **17.97%**, indicating the initial state of waste management efficiency in India.
 
• By **2024-25**, India showed significant progress with the percentage of waste processed increasing to **80.7%** (or 0.807 in decimal format).
 
• This improvement highlights India's advancements in implementing effective waste management practices, contributing towards meeting the targets of the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The correct option **0.807** reflects the decimal representation of the waste processed percentage in 2024-25.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs**, established by the **United Nations in 2015**, consist of **17 goals** aimed at achieving a sustainable future for all by **2030**.
 
• Goal 12 of SDGs focuses on **responsible consumption and production**, including waste management and recycling.
 
• India actively monitors its progress through frameworks like the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Waste Management in India:**
 
 
• India generates approximately **62 million tonnes of waste annually**, of which only **about 60%** is collected, and less than **50%** is processed.
 
• Efforts such as the **Swachh Bharat Mission** and policies on extended producer responsibility (EPR) have been implemented to improve waste processing rates.
 
• Technological advancements, public-private partnerships, and awareness campaigns play a critical role in enhancing waste management.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework:**
 
 
• The **National Indicator Framework** is India's mechanism to track progress against the SDGs.
 
• It includes indicators specific to waste management, recycling, and sustainable urban development.
 
• The framework helps policymakers assess the effectiveness of programs and initiatives aimed at achieving sustainability targets.
 
 
 
• **Waste Processing Technologies:**
 
 
• Modern waste processing includes methods like **composting, recycling, waste-to-energy conversion, and landfill gas recovery.**
 
• India has been investing in **integrated waste management systems** to achieve higher efficiency in processing waste.
 
• Waste-to-energy plants convert non-recyclable waste into electricity, contributing to both waste reduction and energy generation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission:** Launched in **2014**, this initiative aims at achieving universal sanitation and a garbage-free India.
 
• **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR):** Indian policies mandate producers to manage post-consumer waste, especially for plastics and electronics.
 
• **Waste-to-Energy (WTE):** India has set up several WTE plants to process municipal solid waste and generate energy.
 
• **Challenges:** Despite progress, challenges like informal recycling, lack of infrastructure, and low public awareness persist.

questions.question: Which edition of the India-Mongolia joint military exercise, Nomadic Elephant, was held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, from May 31 to June 13, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17th edition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nomadic Elephant** is a bilateral military exercise conducted between **India and Mongolia** to enhance defense cooperation and strengthen mutual relations.
 
• The **17th edition** of this joint military exercise was held from **31 May to 13 June 2025** in **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**.
 
• The exercise focuses on **counter-terrorism operations** and promotes interoperability between the armed forces of both nations.
 
• Participating troops engage in drills for **combat readiness**, including training in operating under challenging environments and exchanging best practices.
 
• The exercise is part of India’s efforts to strengthen ties with Mongolia as part of its **"Act East Policy"**, emphasizing strategic partnerships in the Asia-Pacific region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mongolia-India Relations:**

 
 
• Mongolia and India share historical ties dating back to the spread of Buddhism from India to Mongolia.
 
• India refers to Mongolia as its "spiritual neighbor" and has strengthened cooperation in areas like **defense, trade, and cultural exchanges.**
 
 
 
• **Defense Cooperation:**
 
 
• India provides defense training and equipment to Mongolia under bilateral agreements.
 
• Joint exercises like "Nomadic Elephant" focus on enhancing capabilities for **peacekeeping operations**, disaster management, and counter-terrorism.
 
 
 
• **Act East Policy:**
 
 
• India’s Act East Policy aims to establish closer relations with Southeast and East Asian countries.
 
• Strengthening ties with Mongolia aligns with India's strategic interests in the region.
 
 
 
• **History of Nomadic Elephant:**
 
 
• The first edition of Nomadic Elephant was conducted in **2004** as part of defense cooperation.
 
• It has evolved over the years into a significant platform for military collaboration between the two nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:**

 
 
• Mongolia is strategically located between **Russia and China**, making it significant for regional geopolitics.
 
• India's engagement with Mongolia reflects its broader strategy of enhancing ties with countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
 
 
• **International Cooperation:**
 
 
• Nomadic Elephant is part of India’s broader commitment to global peace and stability through international military collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Training Aspects:**
 
 
• Troops participating in Nomadic Elephant undergo training in areas like **urban warfare**, reconnaissance, and operating in diverse terrains.
